IncidentBot: [PAGE] HIGH TAIL LATENCY p99 surge detected for model redwood-4b-int8-v2 on /v1/stream in eu-west-1. p99=2.05s (SLO=1.0s). Trigger: kernel_fallback_rate and streaming_rebuffer spikes. Paging oncall-sre. Thread started 1769995555

Arnold (oncall-sre): ack. I'm online. Paging ml-infra + eng-runtime. Any recent calibration/quant profile rollouts in eu-west-1 in the past 12h?

Raj (ml-infra): we pushed INT8_CALIB_EU_2026-03-14 to redwood-4b-int8-v2 at 04:01 UTC. Rollout was canary 20% -> 100% by 04:12 UTC. Logs below:
```
2026-03-14T04:01:02Z profile.apply id=INT8_CALIB_EU_2026-03-14 model=redwood-4b-int8-v2 canary=20%
2026-03-14T04:11:47Z rollout complete -> 100%
```

Maya (eng-runtime): metrics show KV cache miss/eviction spikes aligned with p99 upswing around 12:30 UTC. kernel_fallback_count jumped from baseline ~10/hr -> ~380/hr. streaming_rebuffer/sec per 1k req from 0.4 -> 8.1. Some workers show event loop stalls.

Arnold (oncall-sre): dashboards (24h pre-rollout vs now):
- p95: 150ms -> 310ms
- p99: 360ms -> 2.05s
- tail max: ~3.6s
- 5xx errors: stable (<0.6%)

Liz (cust-success): two paying customers (EchoChat, RelayNow) pinged support about freezes mid-stream ~1-3s. No errors, just UX breaks. Contacts: rina@echo, ops@relaynow.

Raj (ml-infra): quick triage: the new INT8 calibration tightened layer-scale quant thresholds to squeeze bit-width but introduced non-monotonic per-token scale adjustments for rare token sequences. The scale-table checksum is included in KV cache keys; checksum variance for certain sequences is causing cache churn and sporadic kernel fallbacks where quantization crosses a boundary.

Priya (eng-runtime): confirm: on some requests kernels detect out-of-range quant values and fall back to reference fp32 path for attention/softmax layers. These fallbacks are expensive and also cause bursts of work that create thread-pool queuing.

Arnold (oncall-sre): mitigation options (fast to slow):
1) rollback INT8_CALIB_EU_2026-03-14 -> INT8_CALIB_2026-03-09 (fast, known-good).
2) per-route routing: flip /v1/stream for redwood-4b-int8-v2 -> redwood-4b-fp16-safe in eu-west-1 (instant routing change, needs capacity check).
3) hotfix to make KV cache key ignore the scale-table checksum (risky correctness-wise).
4) raise worker threads + short autoscale while we investigate (mitigates queuing but doesn't remove fallbacks).
Which do we want to do now?

Rana (ml-infra): my vote: (2) immediate routing flip to fp16-safe for streaming, then (1) rollback as a follow-up. Routing is nondestructive and buys us time.

Sam (ml-infra): agree with Rana. Routing is lower risk and should collapse the tail quickly. I'll still prepare the rollback command in case routing doesn't stabilize p99.

Arnold (oncall-sre): go ahead with (2) and trigger worker scale + then perform rollback if needed. Liz prepare customer comms.

deploy-bot: Queued actions:
```
/routing set --region eu-west-1 --match "/v1/stream" --model redwood-4b-int8-v2 --route-to redwood-4b-fp16-safe --dry-run=false
/infra scale --pool streaming-euw-threads --delta=+30% --ttl=15m
```

deploy-bot: Routing change started (id r-176999-route). Worker pool scale requested.

Maya (eng-runtime): routing flip applied at 12:38:07Z. Canary 10% traffic -> observing routed-canary metrics: p99 ~420ms, p95 ~180ms. Non-streaming traffic still on int8 shows higher fallbacks but streaming tail recovering.

Raj (ml-infra): initiating rollback as a precaution while routing is active: prepared rollback command but will stage it after routing stabilizes.

Arnold (oncall-sre): early cluster telemetry after routing flip and scale:
- overall p95: ~170ms
- overall p99: ~460ms
- streaming rebuffer/sec/1k: ~1.1
- kernel_fallback_count: dropped to ~22/hr for routed streams

Liz (cust-success): notified EchoChat and RelayNow: brief note that we've applied a temporary routing change to reduce latency, investigating calibration issue, will follow up with postmortem. Asked for sample request IDs.

Priya (eng-runtime): follow-ups: I'll add a runtime auto-pause: if kernel_fallback_rate > 3x baseline for 3 minutes during a profile rollout -> pause rollout and optionally auto-route streaming to fp16-safe for that model. Also adding an alert for checksum variance > 0.05% across canary samples.

Rana (ml-infra): my immediate action items: reproduce the checksum variance with synthetic long streams focusing on rare-token boundaries; add unit tests that assert checksum stability across context lengths; change rollout gate to fail if kernel_fallback_rate > 2x baseline in canary window.

Raj (ml-infra): I'll also revisit the calibration generator: introduce monotonicity constraints for per-token scaling and avoid per-layer tweaks that can flip checksum bits for boundary cases.

Arnold (oncall-sre): handing off to Jen for next shift. Summary: INT8 calibration rollout introduced per-token scale variability causing KV cache churn and kernel fallbacks -> streaming p99 spike. Mitigated via per-route fp16 routing + worker scale. Rollback staged. Owners assigned: Rana/Raj (ml), Priya/Maya (runtime), Liz (CS), Arnold/Jen (SRE incident).

Jen (oncall-sre): taking handoff. I'll post the incident ticket and begin the postmortem template. Quick note for next shift: keep routing in place until calibration rollback validated and regression tests added.

IncidentBot: Incident mitigated state set at 1769996399 by Arnold (oncall-sre).
